Use only Node.js built-ins (no npm install). Server - At startup the server checks `PORT`, then reads the data file, then starts listening, in that order. - It listens on 127.0.0.1 at the port in the `PORT` environment variable. An unset or empty `PORT` means 3000. A `PORT` that is not made only of ASCII digits 0-9, or whose value is above 65535, or a port that cannot be bound (for example because it is in use), makes the server write one line of its choice to stderr and exit with code 1. - Once listening, it prints `listening on http://127.0.0.1:` followed by "\n" to stdout, where `` is the port actually bound (with `PORT=0`, the port the OS picked). This line is the only thing the server ever writes to stdout. - Its data lives in the file named by the `DATA_FILE` environment variable, as JSON in a layout of your choice. An unset or empty `DATA_FILE` means `bookings.json`. A relative `DATA_FILE`, the default included, is resolved against the current working directory, not the folder of `server.mjs`. - The server reads the data file once, at startup. If reading it fails with `ENOENT` (the file, or a folder on its path, does not exist), there are no bookings yet. If reading it fails in any other way (for example the path is a directory), or its content is not data in the layout this server writes (for example it is empty or not valid JSON), the server writes `cannot read data file ` followed by "\n" to stderr, where `` is the value of `DATA_FILE` as given (`bookings.json` when it is unset or empty), and exits with code 1 without listening. - After startup the server's memory is the truth: changes made to the file from outside are not noticed. The server writes the data file only when a POST creates a booking or a DELETE removes one, never at startup or for any other request, and it never creates folders. - Every change is saved to the data file before its reply is sent: after a restart with the same `DATA_FILE`, the bookings, and the id the next booking will get, are as before. - If saving a change fails (for example because the data file's folder does not exist), the reply is 500 `internal error` and nothing changes, the next id included. Any other unexpected failure while handling a request also replies 500 `internal error`. In both cases the server keeps running. - Requests that arrive at the same time give the same result as if they had been handled one at a time in some order: of several overlapping bookings sent at once while saving works, exactly one is created and every other one gets 409, and no id is given twice. - Before sending any reply, the server reads the whole request body, if there is one, and discards what it does not use, so the client always receives the reply, the 413 and 415 replies included. API - The rooms are fixed: `Aurora`, `Borealis` and `Cosmos`, in that order. - A booking is a JSON object with exactly the keys `id`, `room`, `title`, `date`, `start` and `end`: `id` is a number, the others are strings. The first booking gets id 1 and each new booking the next integer; an id is never reused, even after deletes and restarts. - Only the parsed JSON of a reply body matters: whitespace and key order in it are free. - A request's path is its request target up to the first `?` (all of it when there is no `?`). Routes compare the path byte for byte, with no percent-decoding and no dot-segment, slash or letter-case normalisation: `/api/%62ookings`, `/api/./rooms`, `/API/rooms` and `/api/bookings/` are none of the paths below. The query, the text after the first `?`, is ignored unless stated, and is decoded as `new URLSearchParams(query)` does. - `GET /api/rooms`: 200 `{"rooms": ["Aurora", "Borealis", "Cosmos"]}`. - `GET /api/bookings`: 200 `{"bookings": [...]}` with every booking, sorted by date, then start, then room in the order above. content.text:
I graded `server.mjs` against the spec's Server, API, Booking rules and Page (`GET /`, `GET /app.js`) sections and against `backend-api.md`, line by line. I found no spec violations. I read the whole of `/root/bench-runs/h4-610ab0b5/server.mjs` (322 lines) and `package.json`. Bash was denied, so I could not run `node --check` or `git diff`. All the findings below come from reading the code. There are no `test/` files yet, by design.

**Spec checks that pass:**
- **Startup:** the order is PORT, then the data file, then listen (306–318). PORT must be all ASCII digits and at most 65535; an empty or unset PORT means 3000.
- **Data file:** only `ENOENT` means "no bookings"; any other read failure, or content that fails validation, gives `cannot read data file <name as given>` and exit 1. A relative DATA_FILE is resolved against the current working directory.
- **Port in use:** a bind failure is one stderr line with `err.code`, then exit 1.
- **stdout:** only the `listening on …` line is ever written there.
- **Saving:** the file is written only by a POST that creates or a DELETE that removes, and before the reply. If saving fails, the next id and memory stay unchanged (`commit` swaps `store` only after `writeFile` succeeds). The promise queue makes overlapping POSTs give exactly one 201, and one failed save cannot block later requests (`queue = run.catch(...)`).
- **Request bodies:** the body is always read to the end, and at most 10001 bytes are kept, for every route and method.
- **Routing:** paths are compared as raw bytes up to the first `?`. The order of checks is: unknown path gives 404, then a wrong method gives 405. `/api/bookings/` and `/api/bookings/1/` give 404; `GET /api/bookings/abc` gives 405. A DELETE id must match `^[1-9][0-9]*$`.
- **Booking rules:** rules 1 to 10 are checked in spec order, including 415 before 413, the BOM being kept, ASCII-only lowercasing of the media type, trimming only spaces and tabs, `trim()` on the title, leap years as year % 4, and the earliest-starting conflict for the 409 message.
- **Listing:** `?date` handling uses `has`/`get` as the spec says. Sorting is by date, then start, then room order.
- **Replies:** the JSON content type is exact, and the 204 reply has no body.

**Findings:**
1. **`createApp` is about 100 lines (203–303)**, against the house limit of 50 per function. It is cohesive, but the request handlers live inside it. Moving `listBookings`, `createBooking`, `deleteBooking`, `route` and `servePage` to module level, with a small store/queue object passed in, would fix this.
2. **The save is not atomic (216).** If `writeFile` fails partway (for example disk full or an I/O error after truncation), memory stays correct but the file on disk can be left truncated. The next restart then fails with `cannot read data file`, which breaks the spec's promise that "nothing changes" across a restart. Writing to a temp file in the same folder and then renaming it fixes this without creating any folders.
3. **The catch-all hides the cause of the 500 (298–301).** The user-facing 500 is correct, but the real error is thrown away with no diagnostic. One line to stderr (not stdout) would keep the reply friendly and still not swallow the error.
4. **The 405 ternary is written out four times (268, 273, 278, 281).** A small helper such as `allowOnly(method, expected, handler)` would remove this. It is minor.
5. **`fail` relies on `return undefined` (100–102, 319).** It exits inside the stderr write callback, so `main` has to `return undefined` to keep going cleanly. This is fine, but an explicit `process.exitCode = 1` together with closing would read more clearly. This is optional and costs no points.

No secrets, no injection paths, and no `console.log`, commented-out code or TODOs. `package.json` matches the spec and `decisions.md`.

## GRADE
Overall: 8/10
Verdict: pass
structure: 8 — clear sections, pure validators, new store objects instead of mutation; createApp holds every handler as a closure
naming: 9 — descriptive and consistent (validateFields, findConflict, commit, serialize, MSG.*)
duplication: 8 — the 405 method-check ternary is repeated four times in route
size: 7 — file is 322 lines (fine) but createApp is about 100 lines, over the 50-line function limit
errors: 8 — startup failures are one line plus exit 1 using err.code; 500s are friendly, but the catch-all hides the cause and a partial save can corrupt the file across a restart
tests: n/a — the testing section writes them
security: 9 — no secrets, body size capped, raw path compared byte for byte, page paths fixed via import.meta.url
leftovers: 10 — no console.log, debug code, commented-out code or TODOs
Fixes:
- /root/bench-runs/h4-610ab0b5/server.mjs:203 split createApp: move listBookings/createBooking/deleteBooking/servePage/route to module level, taking a small store/queue context, so each function is under 50 lines
- /root/bench-runs/h4-610ab0b5/server.mjs:216 write to `${filePath}.tmp` in the same folder, then `rename` over filePath, so a failed or partial save never leaves a truncated data file
- /root/bench-runs/h4-610ab0b5/server.mjs:298 bind the error and write a one-line diagnostic to stderr (not stdout) before replyInternalError, so failures are not silently swallowed
- /root/bench-runs/h4-610ab0b5/server.mjs:268 replace the four repeated `method === X ? … : sendError(res, 405, …)` checks (268, 273, 278, 281) with a single helper
